findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the materialization premise: name the ACTUAL committed consumer that renders rebar.conf.template and installs the mcp-upstream.conf seed to /etc/nginx/ before the first nginx -t (the envsubst render is only a header EXAMPLE, not wired in compose-up.sh; opcert-guard.map.conf is written by materialize-opcert-guard.sh via SSM, not envsubst) — and add that render+copy step to compose-up.sh (or the named boot script) as in-scope work rather than assuming it exists.
evidence: Plan: 'That render step — the SAME `envsubst` consumer documented in the template header that produces `/etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf` and that `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh` uses to materialize `/etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf` — ALSO copies `infra/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` to `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` BEFORE the first `nginx -t`'
search_files 'envsubst' -> only hit is infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template lines 5-11 (a header example comment); no script matches

compose-up.sh (read in full, 194 lines) runs fetch-secrets.sh, materialize-g2p-config.sh, materialize-opcert-guard.sh, and `docker compose up` — it never runs envsubst nor writes /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf

materialize-opcert-guard.sh materializes /etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf from SSM (aws ssm get-parameter -> printf > file), NOT via envsubst — a distinct mechanism the plan folds into 'the SAME render step'
findings.finding: The plan's fresh-boot materialization contract rests on a load-bearing assertion that a single existing, committed host-side step (described as 'the SAME envsubst consumer ... that infra/scripts/compose-up.sh uses to materialize /etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf') will copy infra/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf to /etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf before the first nginx -t. A Grep/Read refutes this: (a) `envsubst` appears ONLY in the rebar.conf.template header as an example comment ('e.g. (in the deploy/boot script)') and in NO committed script; compose-up.sh (read in full) never runs envsubst and never produces /etc/nginx/conf.d/rebar.conf. (b) /etc/nginx/opcert-guard.map.conf is materialized by infra/scripts/materialize-opcert-guard.sh via an SSM fetch->file-write, a DIFFERENT mechanism than the envsubst render; the plan conflates the two into 'the SAME render step'. So the step the plan says already installs the seed is neither the envsubst consumer it names nor is it committed/wired in compose-up.sh.
findings.location: Section 'nginx switchable-upstream materialization (fresh boot + atomic flip)'
scenarios: Fresh boot before foxterrier's first flip: if no committed step copies the seed to /etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf, the glob include is zero-match, the upstream rebar_mcp has zero server lines, and `nginx -t` FAILS ('no servers are inside upstream') — the exact failure the plan says the seed prevents
The AC 'nginx -t passes on the rendered template' cannot be met on the box if the seed-install step is not actually wired
findings.suggested_fix: Stop conflating the envsubst render with the SSM materialize. Either (a) add an explicit envsubst render + `cp infra/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf /etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf` step to compose-up.sh (and list it in File impact), placed before any `nginx -t`/reload, mirroring how materialize-opcert-guard.sh is invoked; or (b) if a separate deploy script owns the envsubst render, name that committed script explicitly and confirm it is invoked at boot before nginx loads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify `logging: driver: journald` on the new `mcp` compose service to match the gerrit/review-bot/opcert services and the S2 observability AC, so MCP container logs land in the host journal.
evidence: Plan lists for the mcp service: 'restart: always', container 'healthcheck', 'stop_grace_period' — but no logging driver.
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml: every existing service ends with `logging:` / `driver: journald` ('Ship container stdout/stderr to the host journal (journald), per the S2 observability AC').
Consistency: an mcp service without the journald driver falls to Docker's default json-file driver, diverging from the box's uniform log-capture convention.
findings.finding: The plan does not specify that the new `mcp` compose service wires the `logging: driver: journald` driver that the three existing services (gerrit, review-bot, opcert) all set per the S2 observability AC, leaving on-box stdout/stderr capture for the new authenticated endpoint unspecified.
scenarios: Operator triages an MCP 5xx or a failed blue-green retire via `journalctl CONTAINER_NAME=compose-mcp-1` and finds no journal stream for the new service.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `logging:\n  driver: journald` to the `mcp` service block in docker-compose.yml, mirroring the other three services.
